snip.t: | Reactive arthritis | Recent GI or GU infection, enthesitis, sacroiliac pain | Usually asymmetric, HLA‑B27 positive, no rheumatoid nodules, seronegative |
| Reactive arthritis | Recent GI or GU infection, sacroiliac tenderness, conjunctivitis, urethritis. | Asymmetric oligoarthritis, HLA‑B27 positivity; sterile synovial fluid. |
| Reactive arthritis | Post‑infectious (GI or GU), asymmetric oligo‑arthritis, may have conjunctivitis or urethritis | No purulent joint fluid; sterile cultures; history of preceding infection |
Look‑alike conditions: crystal arthropathy (gout, pseudogout), reactive arthritis, early rheumatoid arthritis, osteomyelitis, transient synovitis of the hip.
The umbrella includes ankylosing spondylitis, psoriatic arthritis, reactive arthritis, enteropathic arthritis and undifferentiated spondyloarthritis.

qs.q: Which of the following is a classic triad associated with reactive arthritis (formerly Reiter syndrome)?
qs.e: Reactive arthritis is characterized by the triad of arthritis, conjunctivitis, and urethritis. It is a noninfectious inflammatory condition distinct from direct infectious urethritis.
